# Error-handling audit — `entire review` redesign (`review-cutover`)

I traced every `err != nil`, `continue`, and `return nil` in the in-scope diff, and followed the token-parser RunError events through to the orchestrator's status classification. The architecture is, on the whole, deliberate about the silent-failure boundary: the parsers emit `RunError` and keep scanning, and both `Run` (run.go:181) and `RunMulti` (run_multi.go:175) treat `sawRunError` as a hard downgrade to `AgentStatusFailed` even on a clean exit 0. That is correct graceful degradation, not suppression. Most context-builder log-and-continue paths (review_context.go, scope detection) are advisory prompt enrichment where empty output is the right fallback.

That said, I found real issues.

## HIGH

### 1. Stray test artifact committed to the branch — `t1.txt`
Location: `t1.txt` (added by commit `7ce65b97d "trigger 1"`).
Not error handling, but it must not merge. A file containing `test 1` is in the committed range. Delete it and drop/clean the `trigger 1` commit before merge.

### 2. Codex token tailer silently drops a torn final line — `cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/review_tokens.go:59-97`
The tailer accumulates `pending` and only emits on a complete `\n`-terminated line. When `stop` fires (stdout stream ended → parser closing), the loop returns at line 84/93/95 with whatever is in `pending` discarded. A rollout line that codex flushed without a trailing newline before the run ended is never parsed, so the final live-token total can be stale.
- User impact: low-severity — the authoritative totals come from `turn.completed` on the main parser and from post-run hydration (`reviewSummaryTokenEnricher`), so this only affects the live TUI counter, never persisted metadata. But the dropped-tail behavior is undocumented.
- Fix: this is acceptable as graceful degradation, but the function doc (lines 23-38) claims it emits "for every token_count codex writes" — add a sentence noting the final unterminated line is intentionally dropped because `turn.completed`/hydration supersede it. Documenting the drop is the fix; no code change required.

### 3. `parseRolloutTokenCount` parse failures are completely invisible — `review_tokens.go:120-134`
Every `json.Unmarshal` failure collapses to `ok=false` with no logging at any level. If codex changes the rollout `token_count` schema, the live counter silently flatlines at zero and there is zero diagnostic signal — unlike the main parser, whose `default` arm logs unknown envelope types at Debug (reviewer.go:199-201).
- Hidden errors: schema drift in `rolloutLine` / `eventMsgPayload` / `tokenCountInfo`; a `token_count` event whose `Info` is malformed; a partial line that decodes as valid JSON but wrong shape.
- User impact: a future codex upgrade quietly kills live token display with no breadcrumb; whoever debugs it 6 months out has nothing to grep for.
- Fix: in the tailer loop, when a line decodes as a `token_count` event (Type matches) but `parseRolloutTokenCount` returns `ok=false`, emit one `logging.Debug(ctx, "codex token tail: token_count parse miss", ...)`. Don't log per-line for non-token lines (noise), but a shape mismatch on a token line deserves a Debug breadcrumb mirroring the main parser's drift-triage philosophy.

## MEDIUM

### 4. Codex parser emits `Finished{Success: true}` on the same stream that produced `RunError`s — `cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/reviewer.go:204-236`
On a torn line the parser does `out <- RunError{...}` then `continue` (line 146-147), and if the stream still ends with a `turn.completed`, it emits `Finished{Success: true}` at line 233. In isolation that envelope claims success despite mid-stream parse failures.
- Why it's not a defect in practice: the orchestrator's `classifyStatus` checks `sawRunError` (run.go:181, run_multi.go:175) and overrides `Finished.Success`, so the run is correctly marked Failed. The Finished event's `Success` field is effectively dead for the failure decision. This is defensible, but it's a latent footgun: any future consumer that reads `Finished{Success}` directly (instead of going through `classifyStatus`) would be misled.
- Fix (optional, defensive): track a local `sawParseError` in the parser and emit `Finished{Success: !sawParseError}` so the envelope is internally honest. The claude parser (reviewer.go:135-152) has the identical pattern and would get the same treatment. Low priority because the orchestrator is the single reader today.

### 5. `IsZero()` / `applyReviewConfig` divergence can produce a no-op "configured" reviewer — `settings.go:333-336` + `cmd.go:868-879`
`ReviewConfig.IsZero()` now returns false when only `Model` or `ReasoningEffort` is set (good). But the single-agent path gates on `cfg.IsZero()` (cmd.go:361) to reject an unconfigured `--agent`. A config with *only* `Model: "gpt-5"` and no skills/prompt now passes the `IsZero` gate, then `applyReviewConfig` sets `PromptOverride = cfg.Prompt` = `""` (line 875). 
- Hidden behavior: the reviewer spawns with an empty prompt override + model flag and falls through to `ComposeReviewPrompt`'s generic scope-only review. The user asked for "agent X" expecting their configured review; they get a generic pass with no warning that the skills/prompt were empty.
- Fix: this is the same gap `reviewerSkillSuffix` (setup.go:521-532) already flags in the banner ("no skills — generic review"). At spawn time in `runSingleAgentPath`/`runMultiAgentPath`, when a reviewer has neither skills nor prompt, print the same one-line "(no skills — generic review)" note to `out` so the degraded mode is visible at run time, not just at setup time.

### 6. Migration's at-most-one-fixer demotion is silent — `cmd/entire/cli/settings/migration.go:47-61`
When a legacy settings file somehow has two fixer-eligible entries, `MigrateLegacyRoles` silently demotes all-but-alphabetical-first to `RoleReviewer` (line 54-60) with no log and no user notice. The function is called on every `settings.Load`.
- User impact: a user who manually set up two fixers (or hit a prior bug) finds one agent silently changed roles with no explanation. Per CLAUDE.md the migration only persists on next write, so the demotion can also silently re-fire.
- Fix: the role-conflict resolution itself is correct policy, but emit a `logging.Warn` (the caller has `ctx`; thread it in or have the caller log on `changed == true && len(fixers) > 1`) recording which agents were demoted, so the role flip is at least diagnosable. Don't block — just leave a breadcrumb.

- `setup.go:144-148` — `settings.Load` failure proceeds with empty preselects + `logging.Warn`. Correct and explicitly documented as non-fatal.
- `setup.go:446-453` — `DiscoverReviewSkills` error logs at Debug and continues with empty discovered list. Correct for a picker.
- `cmd.go:822-828` — `warnManifestNotWritten` is a model citizen: user-visible reason string + debug-log pointer + sentinel-vs-expected distinction (`logging.Warn` for matcher drift at line 797, `Debug` for the expected no-session case). This is exactly the right pattern.
- `fix.go:549-552` — `mdrender` failure falls back to raw markdown. Correct degradation.
- `cmd.go:536-562` (`detectScope`) — fail-loud on explicit `--base`, degrade-silently-with-Debug on auto-detection. Correct and well-documented.
- `review_tokens.go` WaitGroup-before-close ordering (reviewer.go:128-133) — verified correct; the tailer's sends can't race the channel close.
- Codex/claude RunError-then-continue — verified the orchestrator forces Failed; not a swallow.
